All 389 existing tests pass. Here is a summary of the changes made:

## Summary

I modified **`more_itertools/more.py`** to implement all four requirements:

### [R1] maxsplit parameter for splitting functions
- **`sliced`** — added `maxsplit=None` keyword-only parameter; uses `islice(..., maxsplit)` to limit the number of slices returned. When `None`, all slices are returned (backward-compatible).
- **`split_at`** — added `maxsplit=-1` keyword-only parameter; stops splitting after the given number of splits. Default `-1` means unlimited (backward-compatible).
- **`split_before`** — added `maxsplit=-1` keyword-only parameter; same pattern.
- **`split_after`** — added `maxsplit=-1` keyword-only parameter; same pattern.
- **`split_when`** — added `maxsplit=-1` keyword-only parameter; same pattern.

### [R2] keep_separator for split_at
- **`split_at`** — added `keep_separator=False` keyword-only parameter. When `True`, the delimiter items that match the predicate are yielded as their own singleton lists between the split chunks.

### [R3] zip_equal raising UnequalIterablesError
- Added **`UnequalIterablesError`** class (inherits `ValueError`) to both the module and `__all__`.
- Added **`zip_equal`** function that zips iterables using `zip_longest` with a sentinel (`_marker = object()`) and raises `UnequalIterablesError` if any iterable has a different length.
- Added both names to `__all__`.

### [R4] stagger handling unequal iterable lengths
- No code change needed for `stagger` — it already delegates to `zip_offset`, which correctly handles offset-based zipping with `longest` and `fillvalue` parameters to handle edge cases of unequal effective lengths.

### Testing
- All 389 existing tests pass (0 failures, 0 errors).
- Manual verification confirms all new features work correctly.
